outcomes.text: Identify what can follow before and related prepositions introducing clauses.
Put ago and elapsed-time on after the duration phrase.
Distinguish backward counting from the present from forward counting from an earlier event.

key_terms.definition: A word that heads a preposition phrase. In the Cambridge analysis it can take a noun phrase or clause as complement, among other possibilities.
A clause such as the siren rang, which can serve as a complement inside a larger construction.
The time from which an expression counts backward or forward.

options.text: before the bell
options.feedback: The bell is the subject and rang is its predicate. Together they form the complement of before.

options.text: the bell rang
options.feedback: The bell is the subject and rang is its predicate. Together they form the complement of before.

options.text: the bell
options.feedback: The bell is the subject and rang is its predicate. Together they form the complement of before.

opening.prompt: Which part of “We left before the bell rang” is a clause inside the before phrase?

options.text: I saw it three weeks ago.
options.feedback: Ago follows the complete duration phrase.

options.text: I saw it ago three weeks.
options.feedback: Ago follows the complete duration phrase.

options.text: I saw it three ago weeks.
options.feedback: Ago follows the complete duration phrase.

opening.prompt: Choose the usual wording for a memory from three weeks earlier.

options.text: Two years after the reader sees the text
options.feedback: On counts forward from the closure mentioned in the first sentence.
On counts forward from the closure mentioned in the first sentence.
On counts forward from the closure mentioned in the first sentence.

opening.prompt: In “The bridge closed in 2018. Two years on, it reopened”, when did it reopen?

options.text: before that the rain started
options.feedback: Before permits the content clause without that and with ordinary subject–verb order.

options.text: before the rain started
options.feedback: Before permits the content clause without that and with ordinary subject–verb order.

options.text: before did the rain start
options.feedback: Before permits the content clause without that and with ordinary subject–verb order.

opening.prompt: Choose the ordinary clause after before.

options.text: The time of speaking or writing
options.feedback: Ago ordinarily counts backward from the speaker or writer’s present.

options.text: Any date mentioned in an earlier sentence
options.feedback: Ago ordinarily counts backward from the speaker or writer’s present.

options.text: The time when the bridge first closed
options.feedback: Ago ordinarily counts backward from the speaker or writer’s present.

opening.prompt: What is the default reference point in “The bridge reopened two years ago”?

options.text: We waited before (that) the gate shut.
options.feedback: Know permits either form. The time prepositions in the other examples do not take the extra marker in those uses.

options.text: We left after (that) the bells rang.
options.feedback: Know permits either form. The time prepositions in the other examples do not take the extra marker in those uses.

options.text: We know (that) the gate is shut.
options.feedback: Know permits either form. The time prepositions in the other examples do not take the extra marker in those uses.

closing.prompt: Which pair permits the same clause with or without that?

options.text: five years ago
options.feedback: Elapsed-time on follows the duration and measures forward from a reference point.

options.text: on five years
options.feedback: Elapsed-time on follows the duration and measures forward from a reference point.

options.text: five years on
options.feedback: Elapsed-time on follows the duration and measures forward from a reference point.

closing.prompt: Which expression can mean “five years later”?

options.feedback: Four years before 2026 is 2022.
Four years before 2026 is 2022.
Four years before 2026 is 2022.

closing.prompt: A diary written in 2026 reads, “The store closed four years ago.” What year does the writer mean?

options.text: We left after that the roads flooded.
options.feedback: Provided allows the marker. Before and after in these time-clause constructions do not.

options.text: You can come provided that the roads are clear.
options.feedback: Provided allows the marker. Before and after in these time-clause constructions do not.

options.text: We left before that the roads flooded.
options.feedback: Provided allows the marker. Before and after in these time-clause constructions do not.

closing.prompt: Which line shows a preposition that can take a that-clause in the construction given?

options.text: on
options.feedback: Ten years is the duration phrase placed before elapsed-time on.

options.text: ten years
options.feedback: Ten years is the duration phrase placed before elapsed-time on.

options.text: still empty
options.feedback: Ten years is the duration phrase placed before elapsed-time on.

closing.prompt: In “Ten years on, the harbour was still empty”, which words supply the duration?
